The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica Last updated Mar. 23, 2026 Easter is not a federal holiday in the United States, so federal offices that are open on Sundays stay open, though some private businesses may choose to close. However, it is an official public holiday in several countries, including Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Mexico, the United Kingdom, and many European nations, where government offices, banks, and many private businesses are typically closed. Some places also close for Good Friday and Easter Monday to make a long weekend. Related Questions What is Easter? Why is Easter celebrated? When is Easter? Why is Easter called Easter? The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica Last updated Mar. 23, 2026 Easter is one of the principal holidays, or feasts, of Christianity. It marks the Resurrection of Jesus three days after his death by crucifixion. For many Christian churches, Easter is the joyful end to the Lenten season of fasting and penitence. The earliest recorded observance of Easter comes from the 2nd century, though it is likely that even the earliest Christians commemorated the Resurrection, which is an integral tenet of the faith.
